dedupe_keys.name: tempest database of historical uk extreme weather events ceda

description: TEMPEST (Tracking Extremes of Meteorological Phenomena Experienced in Space and Time) is a database of narrative accounts of extreme weather events in the UK, extracted from letters, diaries, church records, school log-books and other documents held in archival repositories. The entries span more than 400 years, some as early as 1346, and cover places across the UK, with the search focused on five case-study regions: Central England, Southwest England, East Anglia, Wales and Northwest Scotland. Each entry is assigned at least one weather type, dated at least to a year and georeferenced, and many describe the impacts of the event and the responses to it; details of the source documents, authors and repositories are included. It was built by Georgina Endfield, Lucy Veale and colleagues in an Arts and Humanities Research Council project (2013 to 2017) and is archived at the Centre for Environmental Data Analysis as version 3.1 (2017), in XML, under the Open Government Licence, with access for registered CEDA users. Caveats: dates and locations can be imprecise, what counted as extreme depended on the writers, and coverage is uneven across regions and periods. It supports long-horizon historical event catalogues and impact narratives for infrastructure risk and adaptation studies; a related record is EM-DAT.
